slot.brief: Perfectly inelastic collision of two bodies; find common velocity and KE loss

stem: A $4\ \text{kg}$ body moving at $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ collides head-on with a $2\ \text{kg}$ body moving at $3\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in the opposite direction. They stick together. Their common velocity and the loss in kinetic energy are, respectively,

verdicts.working: Taking the 4 kg body's direction as positive, momentum conservation gives v = (4×3 − 2×3)/6 = 1 m s⁻¹. Initial KE = 27 J; final KE = 3 J, so the loss is 24 J.

working:
Taking the first body's direction as positive: $p_i = 4(3)-2(3)=6\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
$v = \dfrac{6}{4+2}=1\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
$K_i = \dfrac12(4)(3^2)+\dfrac12(2)(3^2)=27\ \text{J}$.
$K_f = \dfrac12(6)(1^2)=3\ \text{J}$.
Loss $=K_i-K_f=24\ \text{J}$.

Independent check: Taking the 4 kg body's direction as positive, momentum conservation gives v = (4×3 − 2×3)/6 = 1 m s⁻¹. Initial KE = 27 J; final KE = 3 J, so the loss is 24 J.
solution:
Taking the 4 kg body's direction as positive, conservation of momentum gives
$$v=\frac{4(3)-2(3)}{4+2}=1\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$
Initial kinetic energy is $27\ \text{J}$ and final kinetic energy is $\frac12(6)(1)^2=3\ \text{J}$; hence the loss is $27-3=24\ \text{J}$.
